## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** removing the two `height: visible ? implicitHeight : 0` bindings addresses the binding-loop warnings reported in #11099. They are exactly the two lines the reported warnings point to, and Qt's `Column` already skips invisible children, so empty section titles and status lines still collapse. The `wifiRowsEqual` skip compares all five fields that `wifiRow` projects, so no visible row field stops updating.

The Wi-Fi reconnect half of #11099 does not appear to be addressed by this change, and the causal link the PR describes is not supported by the code paths it touches.

### Reconnect fix is not established by the changed code

In the dependency source, every `connection-activate` that NetworkManager attributes to the omarchy-shell process traces back to explicit user input in the open network panel:

```text
NetworkManager audit: op="connection-activate" pid=<omarchy-shell>
  pid = D-Bus caller of ActivateConnection  (NetworkManager 1.58.1, nm-audit-manager.c / nm-dbus-manager.c)
  └─ Quickshell NM backend activateConnection   (Quickshell 0.3.1, nm/backend.cpp, nm/network.cpp)
     └─ WifiNetwork.connect() / connectWithPsk()
        └─ Panel.qml connectDirectly / connectWithPassphrase
           ├─ row MouseArea onClicked      (open panel, pointer press + release)
           ├─ Enter/Space activateSelected (open panel has keyboard focus)
           └─ password field / Connect button submit
Band pin:  omarchy-network-band -> nmcli (separate process; no-op when band is unchanged)
List refresh / binding loop: syncWifiNetworks() only projects, sorts and replaces rows; no call to connect()
```

A binding loop does not generate input: Qt detects the re-entrant update, prints the warning and returns. A `MouseArea` only emits `clicked` after that same `MouseArea` received the press (the `propagateComposedEvents` exception is not used in this panel), so a delegate recreated under a stationary pointer does not produce a click. #11099 describes reconnects "with no obvious user interaction", and none of the new guards (`opened`, `layoutBusy`, `alreadyConnected`) runs on a path without input. Quickshell's `Network::connect()` and `connectWithPsk()` already return early when the network is connected, so the `alreadyConnected` guard does not prevent an `ActivateConnection` either. It only avoids a "Connecting…" state in the panel.

**Impact:** `Fixes #11099` would close the issue while the cause of the ~15 s outages, its main user impact, remains unidentified. The new docs section and the comments at `Panel.qml` (layoutBusy declaration, section header, status line) and in `Model.js` describe continuous popup resizing, stale clicks during layout thrash and keyboard activation while closed, which the Qt source does not support.

**Suggested change:** keep the binding removal, reference #11099 for the warning half only (for example "Refs #11099") and leave the reconnect half open. Reword the docs and code comments so they describe the guards without the unestablished causal chain. For the reconnect itself, a system-bus capture of `ActivateConnection` calls with their sender during an incident, together with the installed shell plugins and `quickshell --version`, would identify the actual caller.

### The 80 ms `layoutBusy` gate drops legitimate actions silently

`layoutBusy` is set on every real list replacement and cleared by an 80 ms timer, not by layout completion. While it is set, `runNetworkAction` and `setBand` return without feedback, so a genuine connect, disconnect, forget, band change or password submit that lands in that window is discarded. List replacements happen on open, when a scan finishes and on each signal-strength change, so collisions are uncommon but possible. The window also covers only part of the time a click can land on a row that just moved, and keyboard selection is by list index, so Enter after a reorder can still act on a different network once the 80 ms pass.

**Impact:** occasional clicks or key presses do nothing, with no visible reason, in exchange for a guard against a mechanism the source does not show causing the reconnects.

**Suggested change:** consider dropping the gate. If misdirected actions after a reorder are the concern, keeping `selectedIndex` anchored to the SSID across list replacements addresses it without discarding input. If the gate stays, show feedback rather than returning silently.

**Optional test improvement:** the standalone `Column` in `test/shell.d/fixtures/network-layout/shell.qml` has no `height` binding on either child, so its "no Binding loop" check cannot detect the pattern it describes. Either give it the original binding and expect a warning, or remove it. The QML runtime half also reports a passing skip when no compositor is available, so headless runs only exercise the Node source-regex and helper assertions.

**Related:** #12452 removes the same two network-panel bindings plus two identical ones in `shell/plugins/panels/bluetooth/Panel.qml`, so the two PRs overlap.
